items.title: Eni Rovuma Basin and Area 4 partners handover the new kindergarten in Pemba
items.summary: The rehabilitation works transformed the facility into a modern childhood education centre, comprising 6 activity rooms, a dining hall, kitchen, administrative offices, sanitary facilities, recreational areas, and other support infrastructure. The centre is designed to provide a safe, inclusive, and stimulating environment for children with ages between 2 to 5 years “Every child deserves the opportunity to learn in a safe, welcoming and stimulating environment. Seeing this kindergarten ready to serve the children of Pemba is a source of great pride for all of us. This achievement reflects the strength of our partnership with the Government of Mozambique and our shared vision to creating a better future for the next generations”, said Francesco Gasparri, Eni Rovuma Basin General Director The kindergarten is part of an integrated education project that has already delivered other educational infrastructures in Pemba, while also supporting capacity building for teachers and educators, as well as an adult literacy programme.

items.title: Germany reaffirms its commitment to Mozambique with approximately 90 million euros in new projects and encourages reforms
items.summary: For four decades, the Federal Republic of Germany and the Republic of Mozambique have worked together in the areas of development cooperation and humanitarian aid. In both fields, Germany is one of the Mozambican government’s major bilateral partners Photo: Embaixada da República Federal da Alemanha em Moçambique With the new commitments made during the 2026 negotiations, Germany demonstrates strong, ongoing support for critical sectors. Key investment areas include the energy sector and a contribution to the Climate and Development Partnership, aimed at strengthening Mozambique’s climate resilience. This partnership, signed in 2024, supports climate and energy transition policy goals, bolsters climate resilience, and consolidates Mozambique’s position as a regional supplier of renewable energy in Southern Africa. items.title: Dozens of gold prospectors killed in strikes on Egypt-Sudan border, rights group says
items.summary: File photo of gold prospectors in northern Sudan At least 72 civilians who had been prospecting for gold in a border region of Sudan have been killed in air strikes, a regional rights group says Emergency Lawyers, based in the Sudanese capital, Khartoum, said jets targeted the so-called artisanal miners at a popular gold mining sites on Saturday Neither the Egyptian government nor the de facto Sudanese authorities have so far commented Cairo has previously faced accusations of deadly strikes on gold prospectors as part of a crackdown on illicit activity along its southern border Emergency Lawyers noted the previous alleged attacks and said they represented not only a violation of Sudan's sovereign territory but demonstrated the government's lack of control over the region "The deliberate targeting of unarmed civilians violates international humanitarian law and the right to life," it said in a statement on Sunday.
